references.text: Jesus answers accusations of breaking the Sabbath by claiming that the Father works until now, and that He Himself also works. This is the direct context for the claim of 'one work' in John 7:21.

Jesus refers to the 'works' He does as testimony that the Father has sent Him. In 7:21, He points to the specific work (the healing) as proof of His authority, which astonishes (θαυμάζετε) His opponents.

The Pharisees ask if Jesus is a sinner because He does not keep the Sabbath, while others wonder at a miracle. This mirrors the reaction in 7:21 where people are amazed by one work but do not understand its significance.

Jesus says, 'I have done many good deeds for your sake. Which of them will you stone me for?' This is a direct summary of the argument in 7:21 that one work should be enough to recognize His divine mission.
Jesus points out that no one has seen or heard such deeds (works) as He has done, and that these testify about the Father. This underscores the uniqueness of 'one work' mentioned in 7:21.
